To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structural changes in the Indian industry after the reforms were more favorable to productivity than in Mexico.

the industrial sector in both India and Mexico has experienced an increase in productivity levels after the economic reforms, with a greater impact in the case of India, and a process of modernization and restructuring, with a greater concentration of modernization processes in the case of Mexico.

(i) the Indian industry shows a relative process of productive modernization and restructuring; (ii) in Mexico the process of productive moderniza- tion has not been accompanied by the same degree of restructuring; and (iii) in both countries, there has not been a process of structural change that has contributed to the improvement of labor productivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural changes that took place in Mexico and India after similar economic reforms and their effects on labor productivity in the industrial sector.
the evolution of labor productivity in industry after similar economic reforms in India and Mexico.
the following question: What has been the evolution of the industrial labor productivity in the last decade in India and Mexico?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structural change in India has been more positive than the one in Mexico, and that the latter is more dependent on external dynamics.
the structural changes in both countries are still far from being able to guarantee a sustainable process of modernization.
in both cases the economic reforms have had a limited impact on productivity growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in both India and Mexico, there is a relative process of productive restructuring, but with different results in the two countries.

the structural transformation of the industrial sector in Mexico has not been able to generate a process of modernization and productivity growth in the sector, while in the Indian case we can observe that there is a process of productive modernization and a certain restructuring in the sector, although with certain limitations.
the structural change has been more dynamic in India, but it has not been able to improve labor productivity in a significant way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the similarities between the reforms implemented, the results are different in the two countries and the reasons are to be found in their specific characteristics.

, in spite of the fact that the industrial sector has been the engine for growth in both cases, the structural transformations have been insufficient to ensure sustained and balanced productivity growth in the long term, which in turn has been reflected in the low growth of the economy as a whole.
the process of industrialization in the two countries is not converging.
